### Mixed chart
Columns, lines and areas together from one data table, with a second scale for values in other units.

Component ID: `mixed-chart`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/mixed-chart.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/mixed-chart.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.19.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.19.0

Contract SHA-256: `b743f0697a6fcb95953ddb5b22f4b2ba1950faf0ba9127c1858b91d9dafc1267`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Public JavaScript exports: `MixedChart`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: Monthly revenue as columns with a dashed target line, or ad spend with conversions on a second scale, is a mixed chart. Three revenue lines for three plans are a line chart.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: Columns, smooth lines and areas drawn per series from a figure's data table by header class, with dashed lines, a second scale for end series with its own fixed range, x labels, round labels for both scales with .axis, aligned to shared grid lines, a legend, a sparkline modifier, and a pointer and keyboard tooltip with points on the lines.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the columns and SVG are aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#mixed-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="mixed-chart">` takes the same `<figcaption>` and `<table>` as a line chart. `AutoInit()` draws each series by its header cell's class: `column` as columns from zero, `area` as a line over a fading fill, and any other series as a line, with `dashed` for a dashed line. Columns sit behind the lines. A legend names the series and a tooltip follows the pointer from row to row. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="mixed-chart" data-end-min="0" data-end-max="35">
  <figcaption>Revenue ($K), profit margin and customer growth</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Month</th>
        <th class="column">Revenue</th>
        <th class="area end">Profit margin</th>
        <th class="dashed end">Customer growth</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Jan</th><td>$420</td><td>18%</td><td>4%</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Feb</th><td>$460</td><td>19%</td><td>5%</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Also documented

The Mixed chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `mixed-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .mixed-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `mixed-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .mixed-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
